name: Shuttle Sprints (Suicides)
instructions: Set 4 cones in a line at 5 m, 10 m, 15 m and 20 m from your start line.
Sprint to the first cone, touch the line with your hand or foot, and sprint back to the start.
Sprint to the second cone and back, then the third, then the fourth — touching the start line every time.
Drive your arms and stay low out of each turn to accelerate quickly.
Walk back to the start and rest 60-90s between reps.

name: Agility Ladder – Icky Shuffle
instructions: Stand side-on at the start of the ladder with the first square to your inside.
Step your lead foot into the square, then your trail foot into the same square.
Step your lead foot out and diagonally forward, planting outside the ladder past the next square.
Bring your trail foot to meet it outside the ladder, then repeat the pattern into the next square.
Keep your steps light and quick, driving your knees up, and work all the way down the ladder.

name: Agility Ladder – In-In-Out-Out
instructions: Face forward at the start of the ladder.
Step both feet into the first square one after the other (in, in).
Step both feet outside the square, one to each side (out, out).
Move forward to the next square and repeat the in-in-out-out pattern.
Keep your chest up and stay on the balls of your feet for the full length of the ladder.

name: Cone Weave Sprints
instructions: Set 5-6 cones in a straight line, 2 m apart.
Starting at one end, sprint and weave through the cones, cutting sharply left then right around each one.
Keep your hips low and your steps short through each change of direction to stay quick.
Sprint through the last cone rather than slowing down before it.
Jog back to the start and repeat.

name: Hill Sprints
instructions: Find a hill with a moderate incline, roughly 40-60 m long.
Sprint to the top at close to maximum effort, driving your knees and arms.
Lean slightly into the hill and keep your strides short and powerful.
Walk back down to fully recover before the next rep.
Repeat for the prescribed number of reps.

name: Flying Sprints (30m)
instructions: Mark a 20 m build-up zone followed by a 30 m timed zone.
Accelerate gradually through the build-up so you hit top speed right as you enter the timed zone.
Sprint through the full 30 m at maximum speed, driving your arms and staying tall.
Decelerate gradually after the line rather than stopping abruptly.
Walk back and rest 2-3 minutes between reps to keep quality high.

name: Bleep Test (Multi-Stage Fitness Test)
instructions: Mark two lines 20 m apart.
Run between the lines in time with a beep, or a steadily shortening interval if running solo.
Touch or turn behind each line before running back to the other.
Each level shortens the time allowed to cover the 20 m, so your pace increases stage by stage.
Stop when you can no longer reach the line in time — that stage and shuttle number is your score.

name: Jump Rope – Basic Bounce
instructions: Hold the rope handles at hip height with your elbows close to your body.
Turn the rope mainly with your wrists, not your whole arms.
Jump just high enough to clear the rope, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Keep a steady, relaxed rhythm rather than jumping high.
Continue for the prescribed time, resting briefly if your rhythm breaks down.

name: Jump Rope – Double Unders
instructions: Start with the same relaxed stance as a basic bounce, rope turning from the wrists.
Jump slightly higher than usual to give the rope time to pass under your feet twice per jump.
Snap your wrists faster to speed the rope up rather than jumping much higher.
Keep your core braced and land softly each rep.
Break into sets if you miss — quality reps beat a long broken streak.

name: Battle Ropes – Alternating Waves
instructions: Anchor the rope and hold one end in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart in a slight squat.
Brace your core and keep a soft bend in your knees throughout.
Drive one arm down hard while the other rises, creating alternating waves along the rope.
Keep the waves consistent in size and speed rather than slowing over the set.
Work for the prescribed time, then rest.

name: Burpees
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop into a squat and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Kick your feet back into a plank position and perform a push-up.
Jump your feet back up to your hands.
Explode upward into a jump, reaching overhead, and land ready for the next rep.

name: High Knees
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up toward your chest while pumping the opposite arm forward.
Quickly switch legs, landing on the ball of your foot each time.
Keep your torso upright and move at a fast running-in-place tempo.
Continue for the prescribed time, keeping the rhythm quick and light.

name: Star Agility Drill
instructions: Set one cone in the centre and four cones around it in a star pattern, each 3-5 m away.
Starting at the centre cone, sprint forward to cone 1 and back to the centre.
Shuffle sideways to cone 2 and back, then backpedal to cone 3 and back.
Shuffle sideways to cone 4 and back to complete one full round.
Move at maximum controlled speed throughout, keeping your hips low on direction changes.

name: Lateral Shuffle
instructions: Set two cones 5-8 m apart and start in an athletic stance beside one.
Push off your outside foot and shuffle sideways to the far cone without crossing your feet.
Touch the ground beside the cone, staying low in a slight squat.
Push off in the opposite direction and shuffle back to the start cone.
Keep your chest up and hips low throughout, moving as quickly as balance allows.

name: Brisk Walking Intervals
instructions: Warm up with 5 minutes of easy, comfortable-paced walking.
Pick up the pace for 3 minutes to a brisk walk — fast enough that talking is a little harder but still possible.
Drop back to an easy pace for 2 minutes to recover.
Repeat the brisk/easy cycle 4-5 times.
Finish with a 5 minute easy-paced cool-down walk.

name: Steady State Walk
instructions: Walk at a steady, comfortable pace you could hold a conversation at.
Keep a relaxed, upright posture with your arms swinging naturally.
Hold the same easy effort for the full duration rather than speeding up and slowing down.
Build the duration gradually week to week rather than the pace.
Finish by slowing to a gentle stroll for the last couple of minutes.
